page: Microsoft Azure E32d_v4 is an EDv4 family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and contains a 35 MB L3 cache. The system architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), alongside cryptography acceleration via AES.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing a 1229 GB solid-state drive (SSD) for temporary data. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this server type.

In benchmark evaluations, the E32d_v4 demonstrates average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU score is 1427.99, while the multi-core score reaches 29830.81. Memory bandwidth testing shows a read-only small block cached speed of 1662.77 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 47.38 GB/sec. Notably, the PassMark memory score of 2812.46 is classified in the top 25% tier, indicating strong memory subsystem efficiency.

The server exhibits performance limitations under heavy computational workloads. While small-scale language model inference (135M parameters) processes prompts at 1120.49 tokens per second, large-scale model inference (70B parameters) drops to a poor rating of 4.51 tokens per second for prompt processing. Consequently, the hardware profile is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, caching layers such as Redis (which achieved 27.24 million operations per second in testing), and software compilation tasks.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core and local SSD storage, the E32d_v4 is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching applications like Redis, which achieves 27.24 million operations per second.
